story.title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads

facts.text: Reading about all that damage, to both infrastructure and animals, inspired Sara Nozkova (pictured above on the left) to develop a wildlife-deterrent system that works differently from the sirens, lights, fences, falcons, and culling traditionally used to keep animals away from roads, train tracks, airports, and other infrastructure.

That work turned into Flox Intelligence , which spun out of KTH in 2020 and is one of the finalists at this year’s Startup Battlefield 200 pitch competition at TechCrunch Disrupt , taking place this year at Moscone West in San Francisco October 13-15.
Like autonomous vehicles, they use perception systems to sense their surroundings, but theirs are trained on wildlife behavior.

Nozkova says about 150 Flox devices are live in North America, Europe, and Australia at airfields and airport perimeters, road and rail corridors (especially fence ends and crossings along wildlife corridors), national parks, agricultural land, urban areas, mining sites, and critical infrastructure such as electrical substations.
The train, you see, had apparently hit a wild bison at full speed, and the impact damaged the engine so badly that it had to be towed away for repairs.

After spending 13 years working in transportation and autonomous vehicles, Nozkova had learned how quickly the systems we build to navigate roads and other controlled environments fail once nature enters the equation.
Flox also has OEM partnerships with companies that pay an annual fee to deploy its software on vehicles, like trains.

Flox Intelligence , a wildlife intelligence company building AI systems enabling infrastructure to prevent human-wildlife conflict, today announced a €2.5 million ($3 million) Seed+ round to accelerate deployments across North America.
It is building edge-based physical AI that can operate 24/7 in harsh environments, where decisions have to be made in seconds.
The company combines embedded systems, real-time sensing, and applied wildlife science to speak with animals in their own language.
“For decades, we’ve relied on reactive tools — from scare tactics to fences — that don’t scale, don’t learn, and don’t protect the corridors wildlife depends on.
For so many years, we have been fighting wildlife, but what if we could communicate with them instead?

“Flox Intelligence is building a future where critical infrastructure can proactively prevent conflict, where animal movement is respected and safer, and where people and wildlife can finally coexist.

The technology prevents collisions, damage, and disruption across critical infrastructure, including railways, airports, roads, agriculture, and industrial sites, and provides reporting through the Flox Wildlife Platform.
This keeps growing every year as humans take more space, wild animals are pushed closer to urban spaces, and transportation systems get faster, quieter, and harder to avoid.
Flox Intelligence was founded in 2020 by Nozkova and Tomas Becklin.
It was born out of an AI research lab at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm.
The company recently relocated its commercial headquarters to the US.
It is also helping DOT road networks where deer and bison collisions drive injuries, fatalities, and financial losses.
Flox Intelligence claims to be built on a different premise.
It has expanded its operations across the U.S. and Canada, grown its New York headquarters, and accelerated commercial deployments over the past few months.
Ford International Airport, WWF, KWS Group, Boliden, and Alstom.

The startup’s first commercial product, Edge, is an intelligent wildlife deterrent system built for harsh, real-world environments, engineered for multiple species, extreme weather, remote sites, limited connectivity, and long uptime.

Every deployment makes the next one smarter, and collectively, these deployments are building one of the world’s largest non-lethal wildlife datasets and windows into how wildlife moves, adapts, and survives alongside human infrastructure.
